items.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]
items.q: I’ve never seen him except with our writing we’ve become friends.

ctx.x: I wonder if Spiegle Wilcox is in this picture.

Yes he is. I know all those guys in that. That’s Spiegle Wilcox right there. That’s the Doc, they call him Doc Riker. He’s the saxophone player. This is Beiderbecke right there, that’s the trombone player, that’s Bill Challis, that is probably Chauncey Morehouse, that’s Steve Brown the bass player. I don’t know who that is, this is Frank Trumbauer, no that’s the long tell guitar player, I forget his name, I shouldn’t forget it but I’ve forgotten those names. This is Itsy Riskin who is one of the piano players.…

He’s still alive, he stroked and not very well. Paul Mertz wrote a thing, a novelty piano solo called “Hurricane,” which I’ve learned to play back in my early days, and also I found out later that he wrote a song which became quite popular called “In This World of Interesting People I’m Glad There’s You.” And he wrote that under the name of something else. And Jimmy Dorsey and he were the composer and lyricist on it. And somebody said that’s not right because it wasn’t Mertz at all. Well I found out that he wrote…
